about: What the workbench bar does, once for both viewers: Storybook's Playwright suite (packages/components/test/visual/workbench-scenarios.spec.mjs) and Widgetbook's widget tests (packages/solar_flutter/widgetbook/test/workbench_scenarios_test.dart) run every scenario here against their own bar, each through a small driver over a fake of the HTTP contract (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-27-viewer-workbench.md). A step or an expectation a driver lacks fails that driver. Words may differ between the bars; the facts shown may not.

A value { "$fixture": "<name>", ... } is a copy of fixtures.<name> with the object's other keys put over it, resolved in turn. The string "$platform" is the bar's own platform (web in Storybook, flutter in Widgetbook) and "$other" the other one, as a value or as an object's key. packages/codegen/test/workbench-scenarios.test.mjs checks every scenario against the vocabulary below.

Every control in the bar must be one of vocabulary.actions (or, on one platform alone, vocabulary.platformActions: controls the scenarios never name): at the last expectation, and at any naming enabled, disabled or absent, the actions offered are exactly enabled and disabled together. A scenario that presses, chooses, confirms or cancels names the calls it expects last, even none.

fake.health: false: nothing answers on the port (GET /health fails). Default true.
fake.startingTimes: how many times GET /status answers 503 (still starting) before it answers. Default 0.
fake.status: the Status GET /status answers, until an answer or a setStatus step changes it.
fake.inspection: the Inspection GET /component answers, its variant set to the one asked.
fake.controls: the Playground's values the bar is given, by control (what Report sends as controls). Default {}.
fake.answers: by route (status, component, set, keep, undo, approve, unapprove/preview, unapprove, report, send): { answer, status, events, hold } or { refuse: { status, error }, events, hold }. The route's events are delivered first; where hold is true, the answer then waits for a release step; then status (where given) becomes what GET /status answers, and the answer is sent: answer, the body (omitted, the Status now), or the refusal. A GET route takes refuse alone. A POST route not listed fails the scenario; a key not named here fails it too.

steps.press: presses the bar's button of this name, which must be enabled.
steps.choose: { select, option }: opens the Select labelled select and chooses the one option whose words contain option.
steps.type: { field, text }: types text in a field: "reason", the pending edit's reason; "note", Report's note; or "agentNote", the note Send to agent carries with the failing checks.
steps.event: { type, message? }: the service sends this event (busy, changed or failed); the step ends once the bar has asked for the events after it.
steps.setStatus: a Status: what GET /status answers from now on.
steps.release: a route: the answer held there (hold) is sent.

expect.calls: the POSTs sent so far, in order, exactly: [route, body].
expect.reads: the reads sent so far other than GET /events, in order, exactly: ["health"], ["status"], ["component", { name, variant }].
expect.absent: actions not offered (redundant: an expectation naming enabled, disabled or absent, and every scenario's last, also checks that the actions offered are exactly enabled and disabled together).
expect.shows: facts shown, in the bar or the dialog open: each a short phrase, not a sentence.
expect.oneError: exactly one error is shown, and it contains this fact.

serial.about: The routes the service runs one at a time (session.mjs's serial). Unless the scenario gives the route's events itself, the fake sends busy (message "working: <route>", which GET /status answers as busy until the route has answered) when the request arrives, then, once the answer is decided, failed (with the refusal's error) where it refuses, and changed, before it answers.
